issues.label: Appellate reviewability of SJ denial
issues.why: The court must decide whether denial of summary judgment remains reviewable after a full jury trial and final judgment.

issues.label: Proper standard of review (SJ)
issues.why: The court must apply the correct de novo summary-judgment standard and view evidence in the nonmovant’s favor.

issues.label: Proper standard of review (trial)
issues.why: Challenges to the verdict require applying the correct standards for JNOV, directed verdict, manifest weight, and sufficiency depending on the assignments of error.

issues.label: Issue preservation at trial
issues.why: The court must determine whether Gill Dairy preserved arguments via Rule 50 motions, objections to instructions/interrogatories, and evidentiary objections.

issues.label: Harmless-error / prejudice analysis
issues.why: Even if error occurred, the court must assess whether it affected substantial rights and warrants reversal or a new trial.

issues.label: Workers’ compensation exclusivity exception
issues.why: The court must confirm the claim fits the narrow statutory exception to employer immunity under R.C. 2745.01.

issues.label: Elements under R.C. 2745.01(A)
issues.why: The court must ensure the plaintiff proved intent to injure or belief injury was substantially certain to occur as defined by the statute.

issues.label: Meaning of “substantially certain”
issues.why: The court must apply R.C. 2745.01(B)’s definition equating substantial certainty with deliberate intent to injure.

issues.label: Availability of R.C. 2745.01(C) presumption
issues.why: The court must decide whether the evidence can trigger the rebuttable presumption based on deliberate removal of a safety guard causing injury.

issues.label: Definition of “equipment safety guard”
issues.why: The court must determine whether the PTO shaft guard and PTO coupling guard qualify as “equipment safety guards” under the statute/case law.

issues.label: What constitutes “deliberate removal”
issues.why: The court must decide whether failure to repair/replace or continued operation without a guard can legally amount to “deliberate removal” under R.C. 2745.01(C).

issues.label: Omission vs affirmative act
issues.why: The court must address whether an omission (not reinstalling/replacing) can satisfy “remove, lift, push aside, take off, or otherwise eliminate.”

issues.label: Removal by employer or third party
issues.why: The presumption requires employer removal, so the court must determine whether removal by a contractor or unknown person counts and whether employer authorization/adoption suffices.

issues.label: Scope of “deliberate decision”
issues.why: The court must assess whether conscious choice to operate/return to service without guards is enough even if the employer did not physically remove them.

issues.label: Causation for presumption (“direct result”)
issues.why: The court must decide whether the injury occurred as a direct result of the missing guard(s), including which guard’s absence caused the entanglement.

issues.label: Which guard matters (shaft vs coupling)
issues.why: The court must determine whether the PTO coupling guard’s absence alone (or partial shaft-guard absence) satisfies the statutory causation and the jury findings.

issues.label: Multiple missing guards theory
issues.why: The court must address whether removal of one guard is sufficient when other guards were also missing/damaged and how that affects causation and instructions.

issues.label: Proximate cause generally
issues.why: Beyond the presumption, the court must decide whether Gill Dairy’s conduct proximately caused Camara’s injuries under Ohio tort principles.

issues.label: Intervening/superseding cause
issues.why: The court must consider whether Camara’s act of turning the machine on to investigate the leak or any other conduct breaks causation.

issues.label: Employee negligence or misconduct
issues.why: The court must determine whether comparative negligence is barred/irrelevant to intentional tort or affects causation or damages in this statutory context.

issues.label: Assumption of risk / knowing exposure
issues.why: The court must consider whether Camara’s awareness of the hazard impacts liability, causation, or damages under R.C. 2745.01.

issues.label: Employer knowledge of hazard
issues.why: The court must evaluate evidence that management knew guards were missing and appreciated the risk, bearing on deliberate intent and presumption application.

issues.label: Rebuttal of presumption burden
issues.why: The court must confirm the burden-shifting framework: employer must rebut presumed intent and what quantum of proof applies.

issues.label: Adequacy of rebuttal evidence
issues.why: The court must decide whether affidavits/testimony that owners did not remove/authorize removal rebut the presumption as a matter of law or present a jury question.

issues.label: Credibility vs legal sufficiency
issues.why: The court must separate credibility determinations (for jury) from whether evidence is legally sufficient to meet or rebut the presumption.

issues.label: Use of OSHA findings at trial
issues.why: The court must address admissibility/weight issues for OSHA reports/statements and any hearsay or public-record exceptions affecting the verdict.

issues.label: Use of BWC report/quote alteration evidence
issues.why: The court must consider admissibility and permissible inferences from alleged document alteration, including whether it supports intent/knowledge or is unfairly prejudicial.

issues.label: Spoliation-related evidentiary inferences
issues.why: Even though spoliation claim failed, the court must consider whether spoliation-type evidence/instructions improperly influenced the intentional-tort verdict.

issues.label: Jury instruction on intent standard
issues.why: The court must ensure the jury was properly instructed that liability requires deliberate intent to injure (or statutory presumption) and not mere recklessness/negligence.

issues.label: Instruction defining “deliberate removal”
issues.why: The court must determine whether the court’s definition improperly broadened/narrowed R.C. 2745.01(C) compared to controlling precedent.

issues.label: Instruction on “may but not required”
issues.why: The court must assess whether the permissive-inference wording correctly conveyed the rebuttable presumption and did not shift the burden improperly.

issues.label: Consistency of instructions and interrogatories
issues.why: The court must confirm interrogatories and general instructions aligned on elements, burdens, and causation requirements.

issues.label: Validity of interrogatory majority verdict
issues.why: The court must ensure the verdict and interrogatory answers satisfy Ohio rules on civil jury verdicts (e.g., concurrence requirements) and were properly recorded.

issues.label: Interrogatory-vs-general verdict conflict
issues.why: If any inconsistency exists, the court must apply the rule for resolving conflicts between interrogatories and the general verdict.

issues.label: Sufficiency of evidence on removal
issues.why: The court must determine whether evidence (video image, testimony, OSHA statements, repair history) supports a finding that Gill Dairy deliberately removed/eliminated the guard.

issues.label: Sufficiency of evidence on intent
issues.why: The court must determine whether, with or without the presumption, evidence supports a finding of deliberate intent to injure as required by R.C. 2745.01.

issues.label: Manifest weight of evidence
issues.why: If raised, the court must consider whether the jury clearly lost its way in finding deliberate removal, causation, and unrebutted presumed intent.

issues.label: Corporate attribution of intent
issues.why: The court must decide how intent/removal by owners, managers, or agents is imputed to Gill Dairy LLC for statutory intentional tort purposes.

issues.label: Course-and-scope employment
issues.why: The court must confirm Camara was an employee acting within the course of employment when injured, an element of the claim.

issues.label: Statutory interpretation methodology
issues.why: The court must interpret R.C. 2745.01(C) consistent with Ohio Supreme Court precedent, legislative intent, and any narrow-construction principles for intentional tort exceptions.

issues.label: Effect of prior repairs by contractor
issues.why: The court must consider whether removal during the 2016 pump replacement and non-reinstallation can constitute “deliberate removal” by the employer.

issues.label: Duration of missing guard
issues.why: How long the guard was missing (2017–2019) may bear on deliberate decision/knowledge and must be assessed legally and factually.

issues.label: Evidence of warnings and training
issues.why: Manufacturer warnings and any employer training/safety policies may affect knowledge, intent, and causation issues.

issues.label: Damages proof and permissible scope
issues.why: The court must ensure compensatory damages were supported by evidence and properly limited to compensable categories under Ohio law.

issues.label: Damages apportionment categories
issues.why: The court must verify allocation between economic and noneconomic damages if required for review, remittitur, or statutory limitations.

issues.label: Post-judgment relief standards
issues.why: If Gill seeks a new trial or remittitur, the court must apply the correct legal standards and evaluate claimed errors cumulatively where applicable.

issues.label: Collateral estoppel/agency admissions
issues.why: The court must decide whether statements to OSHA/BWC by an owner/manager are admissible as party-opponent admissions and how they affect liability findings.

issues.label: Hearsay within agency reports
issues.why: Even if reports are admissible, embedded statements may require separate hearsay analysis affecting key intent/removal evidence.

issues.label: Authentication of video/image
issues.why: The court must ensure the March 2018 video/image was properly authenticated and fairly represented the machine’s condition.

issues.label: Foundation for altered document claim
issues.why: The court must decide whether sufficient foundation supported presenting the “quote altered to invoice” evidence and related argument to the jury.

issues.label: Closing-argument misconduct
issues.why: If alleged, the court must determine whether counsel’s arguments about alteration/spoliation improperly inflamed the jury and prejudiced the verdict.
